newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO eyes CS/Winterthur's U.S. moves.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO eyes CS/Winterthur's U.S. moves.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Friday it would consider the implications of any sale of U.S. banking assets by Credit Suisse, which earlier this week announced a merger with Winterthur.
But spokesman Jules Prast said there was no need to speculate about any action the Dutch bank would take if the combined Swiss group was forced to sell U.S. assets.

U.S. legislation prohibits a bank and an insurance group which merge from being active in both fields in the United States, forcing Credit Suisse/Winterthur to dispose of either its U.S. insurance or banking operations.

Prast said ABN AMRO, the largest foreign bank in the United Staes with 15,000 staff and 400 branches, had always indicated it would defend its market position as the consolidation process in U.S. banking rolled on.
He said that if the Swiss group put its U.S. banking assets up for sale, ABN AMRO would look at what it meant for the U.S. banking industry and for ABN AMRO itself.
"But, as far as we are concerned, there's no reason now to speculate about any options we would choose," he added.
Analysts said ABN AMRO, which has a reputation as an acquisitive bank, could cast an eye over Credit Suisse's network of U.S. offices serving multi-national corporate clients.
The Dutch bank has similar operations, offering synergies if they were combined.
